claims.text: A read model is data stored in the shape one query needs, written from the write side's changes rather than by the use cases; it can live in the same database as the write side and need not be a separate store.
At stage-2 orders has id, customer_id, placed_at, status and idempotency_key; status is overwritten on each change, so the orders row keeps no past status and no time other than placed_at.

At stage-3 OrderService.CancelOrderAsync calls repository.FindAsync, order.Cancel(), events.DispatchAsync(order), then repository.SaveChangesAsync(); Cancel() records OrderCancelled; CancelOrderAsync does not mention the history.

At stage-3 RecordOrderStatusHistory implements IDomainEventHandler<T> for the six events Order records (OrderPlaced, OrderCancelled, OrderShipped, OrderRefundRequested, OrderRefunded, OrderRefundFailed) and is registered once per event with AddScoped.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: RecordOrderStatusHistory.cs:13-15, ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:36-41, Entities.cs domainEvents.Add x6

claims.text: Mapping event→(name,status): placed→new, cancelled→cancelled, shipped→shipped, refund-requested→refunding, refunded→cancelled, refund-failed→paid; AddRow only calls db.OrderStatusHistory.Add and does not save.
Order has no property referring to order_status_history; OrderStatusHistoryEntry lives in DonHang.Infrastructure and only RecordOrderStatusHistory writes it, only EfOrderHistory reads it.
SaveChangesAsync saves all tracked changes of the DbContext in one transaction by default, so the order's new status and the added history row are committed together or not at all.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Transactions (Default transaction behavior); lesson design.l3.dispatching-domain-events

claims.text: In PostgreSQL a statement that starts after a transaction commits sees that transaction's changes (Read Committed default), so a request after the save sees both the status and the history row.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 13.2.1 Read Committed Isolation Level; lesson backend.l3.eventual-consistency

claims.text: A placed order gets its id only when SaveChangesAsync inserts it; setting the navigation Order on a new OrderStatusHistoryEntry lets EF Core fill order_id in that same save (dependent inserted after principal).
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Changing Foreign Keys and Navigations (fixup); RecordOrderStatusHistory.cs:34 comment

claims.text: OrdersController.History (GET /api/v1/orders/{id}/history) loads the order with FindForReadingAsync, as Get does, only for the OrderOwner check (404 if absent, Forbid if denied), then returns history.ListAsync(id) mapped to OrderStatusChangeDto.
EfOrderHistory.ListAsync filters order_status_history by OrderId, orders by Id (insertion order) and selects Event, Status, OccurredAt into OrderStatusChange; no Order is built, nothing tracked.
Query results that contain no entity types (a Select into a record of scalar columns) are not tracked by EF Core.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Tracking vs. No-Tracking Queries, 'Tracking and custom projections'

claims.text: Migration AddOrderStatusHistory backfills one row per existing order: 'placed', 'new', orders.placed_at. orders holds nothing else about earlier changes, so nothing else can be rebuilt from it.

scripts/design/order-history.sh at stage-3 prints order 7 as shipped in orders with history [placed/new] only; a new order placed then cancelled has history placed, cancelled and two rows (placed/new, cancelled/cancelled).

Keep the read model in the write side's transaction when readers must never see it behind the status; a read model in another database fed by a message consumer suits writes that must not wait, at the cost of readers seeing changes later.
claims.source_hint: outline item 4, misconception 1; depth_notes (trade-off only); lesson backend.l3.eventual-consistency

claims.text: Keep history out of the Order aggregate when no rule of Order needs it: a list inside would travel with every changed order and each new screen shape would grow the aggregate. Opposing context: a rule that depends on past statuses belongs in Order.

A history row exists only for changes that record an event: Order.MarkPaid() sets status paid and records no event, so it gets no row; RecordOrderStatusHistory handles only the six events Order records.
Every OrderService method calls events.DispatchAsync(order) before repository.SaveChangesAsync(); a use case that records an event but does not dispatch it before its save gets no history row.
